TIMEOUTS: these are the values from the research configuration blueprint (Appendix B),
carried over unchanged: 2 seconds for SessionStart, 1 second for every other event.
They are now TIGHTER than they look, because contextctl is a Ruby adapter rather than a
compiled binary and Ruby interpreter startup sits INSIDE the timeout. That is precisely
why the adapters stay light: bin/contextctl requires only Ruby stdlib plus this package,
never Rails and never the mcp gem, and it talks to the already-warm context-agent over a
Unix socket instead of doing work itself. The one-second hook timeout is an outer guard;
the CLI enforces a shorter internal deadline (KIOKU_HOOK_DEADLINE_MS, default 700ms).
OUTPUT CONTRACTS: the events do not share one. Only SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit
emit additionalContext; every other event writes nothing on stdout. Requalify each
event's contract against the installed Claude Code client before relying on it.
The command is given in string form because exec-form support must pass the installed
client capability check first. A hook never invokes Docker, runs tests, scans a
repository or launches a model, and always exits 0.
